finding: The experiment treatment causally increases quality-answer rate
evidence: Causal ATE +3.72pp (95% CI [2.78, 4.66]pp), p=1.18e-14; robust to covariate adjustment; positive in every device/country/tenure segment tested
product_implication: Whatever the treatment changed (evidence points to prompting longer questions) produces a real, generalizable quality improvement, not a segment-specific artifact
recommended_action: Roll out the treatment experience to 100% of users; before full rollout, confirm the exact UI/copy mechanism responsible so it can be preserved in the final design
metric_to_monitor: quality_answer_rate_post (primary); avg_word_count_post and num_questions_post as guardrails

finding: Question length is the strongest known driver of answer quality
evidence: +9.8pp quality rate for >=50-word vs <50-word questions (p=2.6e-74); regression: +50 words associated with +29% more upvotes, controlling for views/topic/device/country
product_implication: Encouraging longer, more detailed questions is a high-leverage, generalizable lever - not dependent on the specific tested treatment
recommended_action: Add composition-time guidance (e.g. a minimum-detail prompt, example placeholder text, or a soft length nudge) to the question-asking flow product-wide, independent of the A/B treatment rollout

finding: 12.7% of users are consistent 'lurkers' who browse/vote but never ask, and this segment cannot be explained by device, country, or tenure
evidence: Logistic regression for is_asker: AUC=0.52, no significant predictors (Step 3); lurkers average 14.7 activity events vs 18.4 for askers (Step 2/3, p=6.7e-174) - active, not disengaged
product_implication: Demographic targeting will not convert lurkers to askers; the trigger is likely contextual/behavioral, not who the user is
recommended_action: Test contextual prompts triggered by browsing behavior itself (e.g. 'ask about this' after repeated views on a topic) rather than broad demographic campaigns

finding: Device type and country do not meaningfully affect engagement or quality after formal testing
evidence: Asking rate by device: chi-sq p=0.94; quality rate by country: chi-sq p=0.51, Cramer's V=0.013 (trivial effect size); both null in regression
product_implication: Building device- or country-specific engagement features for THESE outcomes would not be evidence-based; the EDA-level country spread does not hold up under formal testing
recommended_action: Deprioritize device/country-specific initiatives aimed at question-asking or quality; re-test only if a major UI or localization change ships
metric_to_monitor: asker_rate and quality_answer_rate by device_type/country (periodic re-check)

finding: New users engage identically to established/veteran users, and the treatment works at least as well for them
evidence: Asker rate by tenure: chi-sq p=0.90; tenure vs questions correlation r=-0.006 (p=0.48); treatment effect: New +5.6pp (p=2.6e-5) vs Established +3.4pp, Veteran +3.5pp (Step 4)
product_implication: The treatment is safe and effective from a user's very first days - no onboarding-specific risk, and the largest point estimate of the lift is for new users
recommended_action: Include the treatment experience by default in the new-user onboarding flow rather than only as a post-signup test arm
metric_to_monitor: quality_answer_rate_post by tenure segment; new-user activation rate

finding: Overall platform activity predicts how much users post, not how good it is
evidence: Activity vs questions asked: rho=0.52 (p<2.2e-16); activity vs quality rate: r=0.02 (n.s., Step 2/3)
product_implication: Engagement/gamification features (streaks, notifications, badges) will likely grow posting VOLUME but will not by themselves improve quality, and could dilute average quality if shipped alone
recommended_action: Pair any future volume-boosting feature with a quality-focused lever (e.g. the word-count nudge above) rather than shipping engagement gamification in isolation
metric_to_monitor: quality_answer_rate tracked alongside any volume/engagement feature launch

finding: Daily/weekly engagement is flat with no organic growth or decline across the full observation window
evidence: Mean DAU ~3,116, range 2,899-3,360 across 60 days; no day-of-week seasonality; apparent week-edge dips confirmed as calendar-boundary artifacts, not real (Step 2)
product_implication: This 2-month period is a clean, stable baseline for evaluating future experiments, but shows engagement per existing user is not growing on its own
recommended_action: Use this period's flat KPI averages as the reference baseline for judging future feature launches; treat user growth as an acquisition problem, not an assumption of organic engagement lift
metric_to_monitor: DAU/WAU trend vs. this baseline after any future launch
